WASP-19 is an interesting planet that has a very deep eclipse in the visible bands and is consistent with a super-solar carbon abundance.

the broadband emission spectrum of WASP- 19b favours a carbon-rich composition and a flat temperature profile.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the emission spectrum of WASP- 19b is well explained by current atmosphere models and is not indicative of any new physical phenomena.

the broadband spectrum is a powerful tool for characterizing exoplanet atmospheres and that future observations in z-band and beyond will be important for constraining the atmospheric chemistry and dynamics of hot Jupiters.
